mainTopic: Who may work and manage someone else's abandoned, captive's, or minor's property, and how they are paid
overview: The גמרא first explains the difference between נטושים (land the owners had to leave) and רטושים (land the owners left by choice), with a פסוק for each. It then asks which kind of property the teaching 'we pay him like an אריס' refers to. It settles on נטושים according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the worker is not removed, as with שבויין, but he gets only an אריס's pay. The גמרא explains this payment with the case of a husband of a קטנה. He cannot rely on keeping the property, so the רבנן paid him to keep him from ruining it. Next, the word וכולן is shown to include רב נחמן's runaway, who is treated like a captive when he flees a murder charge, but not when he flees a tax. שמואל adds that a steward harvests a captive's ripe crops before a relative takes over, since permanent stewards are not appointed for adults. Finally, רב הונא limits who may manage a captive's or a minor's property, and רבא begins to learn from this that no one can make a חזקה on a minor's property.

steps.title: What 'נטושים' and 'רטושים' mean
steps.stepSummary: נטושים are fields the owners left against their will; רטושים are fields the owners left by their own choice. Each meaning is supported by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'נטושים' means land left against the owners' will, as it says about שמיטה: 'you shall let it rest and leave it (וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ)'. That is a forced release by the King. 'רטושים' means land left by the owners' own choice, as it says: 'a mother was left (רֻטָּשָׁה) with her children'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between two words in the ברייתא: נטושים (left by force) and רטושים (left by choice).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for נטושים comes from שמיטה, where the farmer must leave his field because הקב״ה commands it, not because he wants to. The proof for רטושים comes from הושע, where the men left their families behind, a leaving that was their own choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Property the owners had to leave, against their will
Property the owners left by their own choice
Against their will, by force
By their own choice
A release forced by the King's order

steps.confusionAlert: The two words sound almost the same (נ versus ר), but they mean opposite things for the owner: forced leaving versus choosing to leave. Keep them straight, because the rest of the sugya depends on it.

phrases.english: 'Netushim' are those left against their will,
as it is written: 'And the seventh year you shall release it and leave it' –
that is a release forced by the King.
phrases.notes: The King here is הקב״ה. The farmer leaves his field during שמיטה because he is commanded to.

phrases.english: 'Retushim' are those left by their own choice,
as it is written: 'A mother was left with her children.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of what נטושים and רטושים mean in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נטושים means leaving by force (from the שמיטה פסוק); רטושים means leaving by choice (from the הושע פסוק).

steps.title: A teaching: everyone who works such a field is paid like a sharecropper
steps.stepSummary: A תנא teaches that in all these cases, the worker is paid the way an אריס (sharecropper) would be paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: and for all of them, we pay them as we would pay a sharecropper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short teaching that someone who works another person's abandoned field is paid like an אריס. This sets up the next question: which kind of field is it talking about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אריס is a sharecropper who gets a set share of the crop for his work. The teaching says 'all of them' without saying which properties it means, and that gap is what the גמרא will now explore.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a teaching of the תנאים)
We estimate, we pay based on an appraisal
A sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: It was taught: And for all of them, we pay them like a sharecropper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new teaching about the same three kinds of property
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who works these properties is paid like an אריס.

steps.title: Which property does this teaching mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the properties in the ברייתא the teaching about the sharecropper refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: To which one does this refer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: which property does 'all of them' refer to? It is setting up a test of each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of three kinds of property: נכסי שבויין, רטושים, and נטושים. The גמרא will now try each one to see which fits the 'pay him like an אריס' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? To which case does this refer?

phrases.english: To which one does this refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the teaching from step 2 is talking about
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which property (שבויין, רטושים, or נטושים) does the 'like an אריס' rule apply to?

steps.title: It can't mean captives' property
steps.stepSummary: With שבויין the worker already gets more than an אריס, so the teaching would be pointless there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to captives' property: now that he is 'quick and gains', is there any need to say he gets paid for what he improved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, captives' property, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For נכסי שבויין the ברייתא already said the worker is 'זריז ונשכר', meaning he keeps what he gains, which is better than an אריס's share. So there would be no reason to teach that he gets an אריס's pay. That is obvious and even less than he really gets.

keyTerms.meaning: Captives; here, property of owners taken captive
He was quick and he gains, so he keeps his profit
Is it necessary to say?

phrases.english: If you say it refers to captives' property,
now that he is 'quick and gains',
is it necessary to say he gets paid for what he improved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the teaching as referring to נכסי שבויין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Captives' property already gives the worker more than an אריס, so teaching that he gets an אריס's pay would be needless.

steps.title: It can't mean forsaken property either
steps.stepSummary: With רטושים the worker is removed from the field, so he isn't treated like an אריס at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to forsaken property. But it teaches that 'we remove them from his hands'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, רטושים, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that for רטושים the court removes the field from the worker. Someone who is pushed out like that doesn't have the protected status of an אריס, so the teaching can't be about רטושים.

keyTerms.meaning: We take them out of his possession
It teaches (quoting the ברייתא)

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to forsaken property –
but it teaches: 'We remove them from his hands'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer and immediately rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the teaching as referring to רטושים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רטושים the worker is removed, which doesn't match the status of an אריס.

steps.title: So it must mean abandoned property
steps.stepSummary: With the other two ruled out, the גמרא suggests the teaching is about נטושים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to abandoned property.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out שבויין and רטושים, the גמרא proposes the last option: נטושים. This sets up the next question about whose opinion that fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only נטושים is left. The question now is whether this choice fits any תנא's view of נטושים, since the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings a new suggestion after one is rejected)

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to abandoned property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the third and final possible answer to step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'like an אריס' rule refers to נטושים.

steps.title: Whose opinion fits abandoned property?
steps.stepSummary: Neither the רבנן nor רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to fit: the רבנן remove the worker, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats נטושים like שבויין, which pays more than an אריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say the רבנן, they say we remove him. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he says: I heard that abandoned property is like captives' property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the נטושים answer by showing it doesn't seem to match either side of the argument about נטושים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the worker on נטושים is removed, which is the same problem as רטושים. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, נטושים are like שבויין, which brings back the problem from step 4: he would already get more than an אריס.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
The Sages (the majority view)
I heard (a tradition I received)

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say according to the Rabbis –
but they say we remove it from his hands.
If according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel –
but he says: I heard that abandoned property is like captives' property.
phrases.notes: If it's like שבויין, the problem from step 4 comes back: he should get more than an אריס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'like an אריס' rule refers to נטושים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן remove the worker from נטושים, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל equates נטושים with שבויין, so neither view matches an אריס's pay.

steps.title: Like captives' property in one way, but not in another
steps.stepSummary: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, נטושים are like שבויין in that the worker isn't removed, but unlike שבויין in that he is paid only like an אריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like captives' property, but not exactly captives' property. Like captives' property in that we don't remove him. Not exactly captives' property, because there he is 'quick and gains', while here we pay him like a sharecropper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the teaching follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who compared נטושים to שבויין only in one respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כִּשְׁבוּיִין' (LIKE captives) means similar, not identical. The similarity is that the worker stays on the field. The difference is his pay: with שבויין he keeps his gains, but with נטושים he gets only an אריס's share.

keyTerms.meaning: Like captives' property, but not fully the same
There / here (comparing two cases)
We estimate his pay for him

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the worker is removed from רטושים. On נטושים, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he stays but is paid like an אריס. On שבויין, he stays and keeps his gains (זריז ונשכר).

phrases.english: Like captives' property, but not captives' property.
Like captives' property – in that we don't remove them from his hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שְׁבוּיִין – דְּאִילּוּ הָתָם זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר,
phrases.english: but not captives' property – because there he is 'quick and gains',
while here we pay him like a sharecropper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 7 by narrowing what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison: 'like' means similar in one respect, not identical
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats נטושים exactly like שבויין in every way
steps.terutzMaskana: נטושים match שבויין only in that the worker isn't removed. His pay is that of an אריס.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'like an אריס' teaching is about נטושים, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Why is this different from a husband who spends on his wife's property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the payment to the worker from a משנה where a husband who spends on his wife's property gets nothing back.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned: if a man spends money on his wife's property, whether he spent a lot and ate a little, or spent a little and ate a lot, what he spent is spent and what he ate is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from step 8 that the worker on נטושים gets paid like an אריס. It points to a משנה where a husband who improves his wife's property gets no repayment at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the husband works on property that is not fully his, yet he is not paid for what he spent. So why should the worker on abandoned land be paid like an אריס? Both of them are improving someone else's property on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A formula for challenging a ruling by comparing it to another case
Expenses spent to improve a field
His wife's property, which she owns while he eats the produce
A little

phrases.english: And what is different from that which we learned:
One who spends expenses on his wife's property,
phrases.notes: This is land the wife owns while the husband eats the produce. If the marriage ends, she takes it back.

phrases.english: whether he spent a lot and ate a little,
or spent a little and ate a lot —
what he spent, he spent,
and what he ate, he ate.
phrases.notes: In other words, nobody pays anybody back. He gets no refund for his spending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 8 that the worker on נטושים is paid like an אריס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the worker on נטושים gets paid like an אריס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A husband who improves property that is not fully his gets nothing back, so the worker on abandoned land should also get nothing.

steps.title: The worker is like a husband of a minor wife
steps.stepSummary: The case is compared instead to a husband of a קטנה, who is paid like an outsider because he cannot rely on keeping the property. The רבנן arranged payment so he will not neglect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is only like what we learned: one who spends on the property of his minor wife is treated like someone who spends on a stranger's property. So we see that since he cannot be sure, the רבנן arranged things for him so he will not ruin the property. Here too, the רבנן arranged things for him so he will not ruin it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the right comparison is not a regular husband but a husband of a קטנה (a minor wife). He does get paid back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular husband is secure that the property is his to use, so he improves it for himself and needs no refund. A husband of a קטנה cannot count on the marriage lasting, and the worker on abandoned land cannot count on keeping the field. The רבנן promised both of them payment so they would not neglect or ruin the property.

keyTerms.meaning: His minor wife, married only by rabbinic law
He cannot rely on it; he isn't confident it will stay his
The רבנן made an enactment for his benefit
To ruin them, to let the property go to waste

steps.whatToRemember: Payment like an אריס is a rabbinic arrangement for someone who cannot rely on keeping the property. It keeps him from neglecting it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the reason behind the whole rule: the worker's lack of security is what earns him payment.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לְהָא דִּתְנַן:
phrases.english: This is comparable only to that which we learned:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא הוֹצָאוֹת עַל נִכְסֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ קְטַנָּה –
phrases.english: One who spends expenses on the property of his minor wife —
is like one who spends on someone else's property.
Evidently: since he cannot rely on it,
phrases.notes: She can end the marriage, so he can't be sure her property will stay in his hands.

phrases.english: the Rabbis made an enactment for him
so that he will not ruin the property,
here too the Rabbis made an enactment for him
so that he will not ruin the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לְהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by finding a better comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-comparison: the case matches a different משנה (the husband of a קטנה), not the regular husband.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worker on abandoned land is like a regular husband and should get nothing back.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is like a husband of a קטנה, who cannot rely on keeping the property, so the רבנן arranged payment so he will not ruin it.

steps.title: What does the word 'all of them' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the word וכולן in the ברייתא adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for all of them, we appraise them like an אריס.' What does 'all of them' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a word in the ברייתא: וכולן, 'all of them.' It asks what additional case this word is meant to bring in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the steps before, the payment like an אריס seems to apply only to נטושים. So the word 'all' looks extra, and the גמרא assumes it must be adding some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them
We appraise, estimate the value
To include what? A formula asking what an extra word adds

phrases.english: "And all of them are appraised like a sharecropper" —
"all of them" comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the payment to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which additional case the word וכולן includes.

steps.title: The answer begins: שמואל's rule about a captive's property
steps.stepSummary: To answer what וכולן includes, the גמרא first quotes שמואל: the court puts a relative in charge of a captive's property, but not if the owner left on purpose. This is the background for רב נחמן's runaway case, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: for a captive who was taken captive, the court brings in a relative to manage his property. If he left on his own, the court does not bring in a relative to manage his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting שמואל's rule about putting a relative in charge of a captive's property. This sets up רב נחמן's own ruling about a runaway, which is the case וכולן comes to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner is taken captive against his will, the court protects his property by appointing a relative to run it. If the owner left on his own, he chose to leave his property, so the court does not step in.

keyTerms.meaning: A captive
We bring down, appoint someone onto the property
A relative
He left knowingly, by his own choice

steps.confusionAlert: Two cases are in play here. A שבוי (taken by force) gets a relative appointed. Someone who יצא לדעת (left on purpose) does not.

phrases.english: To include this,
which Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
a captive who was taken captive —
we bring a relative down onto his property,
phrases.notes: The court appoints the relative to look after and work the land while the owner is gone.

phrases.english: if he left of his own will,
we do not bring a relative down onto his property.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וכולן includes the case built on שמואל's rule: רב נחמן's runaway (בורח), who is treated like a captive in that a relative is put in charge of his property, but whose worker is paid like an אריס.

steps.title: רב נחמן: one who runs away is like a captive
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules on his own that a בורח is treated like a שבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן himself said: one who runs away is like a captive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רב נחמן's own ruling: someone who runs away is treated like a captive, so a relative is appointed over his property too. This runaway is the case that וכולן ('all of them') adds to the 'paid like an אריס' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new case beyond שמואל's ruling. A runaway might seem like someone who left on purpose, but רב נחמן puts him in the captive category. That sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: His own, in his own name
One who runs away, flees

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said on his own:
one who flees is like a captive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends שמואל's captive rule to a runaway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בורח is treated like a שבוי, so a relative is appointed over his property.

steps.title: Runs away because of what?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of runaway רב נחמן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who runs away because of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what reason for running away רב נחמן has in mind. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who runs away might look like someone who left on purpose, and for him no relative is appointed. So the reason he fled matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of what? For what reason?

phrases.english: One who flees — because of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of רב נחמן's ruling in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the runaway fled, so we know when he counts as a captive.

steps.title: He runs away to escape a murder charge
steps.stepSummary: Fleeing a tax counts as leaving on purpose, so רב נחמן must mean someone fleeing a murder charge.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he ran away because of a tax, that is the same as leaving on purpose. Rather, it means one who runs away because of a murder accusation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out a tax runaway, because he left by choice. It concludes that רב נחמן means someone running for his life from a murder accusation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Running from a tax is a free choice to avoid paying, so it falls under יצא לדעת, and no relative is appointed. Running from a deadly charge is forced, like being taken captive, so it counts as a שבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, a proposal that is about to be rejected
A tax, a head tax
Here, an accusation of murder

steps.whatToRemember: A runaway counts as a captive only when he was forced to flee, like from a murder charge. Running from a tax counts as leaving by choice.

phrases.english: If we say because of a tax —
that is the same as leaving of his own will,
phrases.notes: This points back to שמואל's case in step 12: if he left by choice, no relative is appointed.

phrases.english: rather, it means one who flees because of a murder accusation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14, ruling out one option and settling on another.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בורח is one fleeing a murder accusation, which is forced like captivity. One fleeing a tax counts as יצא לדעת.

steps.title: שמואל: A steward harvests the captive's ripe crops first
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that when a captive leaves crops ready to harvest, the בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס to harvest them, and only then lets a relative take over the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If a person was taken captive and left grain ready to cut, grapes ready to pick, dates ready to cut, or olives ready to harvest, the court steps in and appoints a steward. The steward does the harvesting, and only after that does the court put a relative in charge of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about a captive whose crops are ready to harvest. First a court-appointed steward harvests, and only afterward a relative takes over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned that a relative is put in charge of a captive's property. שמואל adds an extra step for ripe crops: a steward handles the urgent harvest first. Only after the harvest is done does the regular arrangement of a relative managing the land begin.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain still in the field
The court steps in to take care of his property
A steward or guardian appointed by the court to manage property
They put a relative in charge of the property

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A captive who was taken captive
and left standing grain to be reaped,
grapes to be harvested, dates to be cut,
olives to be picked —
the court goes down to his property
and appoints a steward,
and he reaps, and harvests, and cuts, and picks,
and afterward they put a relative in charge of his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new detail to the topic of a captive's property: what happens when the crops are ready to harvest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For ripe crops of a captive, the court first appoints a steward to harvest, then puts a relative in charge.

steps.title: Why not keep the steward permanently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if a steward can be appointed, why not leave him in charge forever instead of handing the land to a relative?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the court appoint a steward forever!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's ruling: if the court can appoint a steward, why switch to a relative at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a steward was good enough for the harvest, it seems he should be good enough to keep managing the property. This challenges the need for the second stage of handing it to a relative.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him appoint (a challenge: why not do it this way?)
Always, permanently

phrases.english: Let them appoint a steward permanently!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two-stage process in שמואל's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that after the harvest, a relative takes over
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a steward is allowed at all, there seems to be no reason to replace him with a relative.

steps.title: Stewards are not appointed for adults
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a court does not appoint a permanent steward for an adult; the steward was only for the urgent harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not appoint a steward for 'bearded ones,' meaning adults.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the court's normal practice is not to appoint stewards for grown-ups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Appointing an אפוטרופוס is something the court does for those who can't care for themselves, like orphans. The captive is an adult, so the steward was only a short-term fix for crops that would otherwise be ruined; after that, the regular arrangement with a relative applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'bearded ones', meaning adults
We do not appoint

phrases.english: A steward for bearded ones
phrases.notes: "Bearded ones" means grown-ups. Stewards are normally set up only for orphans.

phrases.english: we do not appoint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the use of a steward to special cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A steward could manage the captive's land permanently.
steps.terutzMaskana: Courts don't appoint stewards for adults; the steward was only for the urgent harvest.
steps.whatToRemember: For a captive's ripe crops: a steward harvests first, then a relative manages, because permanent stewards are not appointed for adults.

steps.title: רב הונא's three limits on who may manage property
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules: a minor is not put in charge of a captive's property, a relative is not put in charge of a minor's property, and a 'relative through a relative' is not put in charge of a minor's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The court does not put a minor in charge of a captive's property, nor a relative in charge of a minor's property, nor a 'relative because of a relative' in charge of a minor's property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives three rules about people the court will NOT put in charge of property. The reasons come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These rules limit the general practice of putting a relative in charge. A minor can't manage a captive's land, and when the owner is a minor, relatives are kept away from his land.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor (a child under בר/בת מצוה age)
The property of a captive
A 'relative because of a relative': someone connected only through another relative

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
They do not put a minor in charge of a captive's property,
nor a relative in charge of a minor's property,
nor a relative because of a relative
in charge of a minor's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from שמואל's ruling to a new set of limits on who may manage property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No minor manages a captive's property; no relative, and no relative-through-a-relative, manages a minor's property.

steps.title: The reasons behind each of רב הונא's rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: a minor might damage the property; a 'relative through a relative' is a half-brother's maternal brother; and a relative might take over the land because the minor won't protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor is not put in charge of a captive's property, because he might ruin it. A 'relative because of a relative' is not put in charge of a minor's property: this means a maternal brother (of the minor's half-brother). A relative is not put in charge of a minor's property, because the minor won't protest, and the relative may come to claim ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through רב הונא's three rules and explains the worry behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule one is about care: a child may waste or ruin the land. The other two are about ownership: a relative, or someone connected through a relative, might later claim the land is his, and a minor is too young to object in time.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe he will ruin them (the property)
Brothers from the mother's side
Protests (objects to someone using his land)
To take hold of it as owner (make a claim of ownership)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא explains רב הונא's rules in a different order than he said them: the 'relative through a relative' comes second here, and the plain relative comes last.

phrases.english: They do not put a minor in charge of a captive's property,
because he might ruin it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָרוֹב מֵחֲמַת קָרוֹב לְנִכְסֵי קָטָן,
phrases.english: And not a relative because of a relative in charge of a minor's property,
this is the case of a maternal brother.
phrases.notes: Picture the minor's half-brother on his father's side, who has a brother from his mother. That man isn't related to the minor, but could claim he inherited the field.

phrases.english: And not a relative in charge of a minor's property,
since he (the minor) does not protest —
he (the relative) will come to claim ownership of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹרִידִין קָטָן לְנִכְסֵי שָׁבוּי, דִּלְמָא מַפְסֵיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for each of רב הונא's three rules.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רב הונא make each of these three rules? (implied)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A minor may ruin a captive's land; a half-brother's maternal brother, or a relative, might claim the minor's land as his own, since the minor won't protest.

steps.title: רבא: No one gains ownership of a minor's property by using it
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from רב הונא that a person cannot establish a חזקה (ownership claim through use) on a minor's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from רב הונא's words that one cannot gain a חזקה in a minor's property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a new rule out of רב הונא's statement: using a minor's property does not give anyone a claim of ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only kept relatives away from a minor's land, so a stranger may manage it. רבא infers that a stranger isn't feared because nobody can make a חזקה on a minor's property at all. Relatives must be kept away for a different reason, and רבא's statement continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (we can conclude from this)
One cannot establish a חזקה (ownership claim based on using the property for years)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a practical rule: even years of using a minor's land do not prove ownership, which protects orphans' property.

phrases.english: Rava said,
learn from Rav Huna's statement:
one cannot establish ownership through use of a minor's property,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new legal rule out of רב הונא's ruling just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה cannot be established on a minor's property.
